question.answer: interactions.review with params conversationId and requestRef, body.answer (body.data accepted); a single_string form takes the text, a multi-field form takes one JSON object, and the answer is validated against requested_schema before it is sent; a successful answer is the state transition, because the answered question leaves the window and no further frame is published for it
question.answerable: only the newest question of the open conversation is answered; any other reference answers 409 NOT_PENDING and never reaches the agent, and a question whose schema this host cannot read answers 501 QUESTION_UNSUPPORTED

raw_events.content: one bounded, control-stripped line '[event type] title status raw' for every event the chat has no row for; the rows the host reports through routes of their own stay silent: the turn boundary (complete), context usage (usage, read through usage.read) and the resolved interaction rows

challenges.read: GET /api/challenges -> data.challenge {id, host_id, host_name, kind, message, secret}, or null while no connection asks for input; kind is host_key, password or key_passphrase, host_id is null once that host is gone, and no credential is ever part of this payload
challenges.answer: POST /api/challenges/:challengeId/answer with body.answer; a host_key challenge continues on 'accept' and cancels on anything else, an omitted or empty answer cancels the request, and the answer is never stored, logged or echoed back; 409 CHALLENGE_NOT_PENDING for an id that is no longer the pending one

messages_before: GET /api/conversations/:conversationId/messages/before?before=<cursor>&limit=n loads one older page from the history store and answers it in the messages.list page shape, with has_more_after true because the caller still holds the newer part; 409 HISTORY_EXHAUSTED when the product holds no older page, 500 HISTORY_LOAD_FAILED when it cannot be read, 422 INVALID_CURSOR when the cursor is not in the loaded window
conversations_create: POST /api/conversations with params hostId and body.agent plus body.cwd (agent and cwd are accepted as params too); data is the created conversation row plus session_id (the Agent's own native id), agent, cwd and created=true; 404 HOST_NOT_FOUND, 422 AGENT_UNKNOWN or INVALID_CWD, 409 SESSION_CREATE_FAILED carrying the repository's own reason (a directory the host cannot use fails as itself), 409 SESSION_ID_UNKNOWN when the Agent returned no native id
terminal_open: POST /api/conversations/:conversationId/terminal or POST /api/hosts/:hostId/terminal -> data {host_id, host_name, agent, cwd, target, command}, plus conversation_id and session_id on the conversation path, the command being the product's own terminal route command for this host's Agent target, built by ShellCommands.start and wrapped once for that target; neither route is a GET because the caller names a directory in the request body, and neither launches anything; the target is one conversation — whose Agent, session id and working directory the host reads from its own index, so it does not have to be open — or one saved host, which has none of its own: its Agent is the Agent of the conversation this product holds for that host while there is one, otherwise the first Agent that host's probe found installed, and its directory is body.cwd, which replaces the conversation's own directory when the conversation path sends one; 422 INVALID_CWD without a usable body.cwd for a host target or for a non-string one, 422 TERMINAL_TARGET_UNKNOWN naming neither target, 409 WORKSPACE_UNKNOWN without a usable directory for a conversation, 409 AGENT_UNAVAILABLE for a host holding no Agent any probe found, 404 HOST_NOT_FOUND or CONVERSATION_NOT_FOUND for an unknown target, 501 TERMINAL_UNSUPPORTED for a target this app has no shell entry for; no credential is ever part of this payload
terminal_command: POST /api/conversations/:conversationId/terminal/command or POST /api/hosts/:hostId/terminal/command -> the same answer as terminal_open, with the same body, the same directory rules and the same refusals: on this host one terminal route runs the Agent's own TUI, so the command is the ShellCommands.start command of that conversation or that host's Agent; the route is named separately so the caller can hand it to the terminal as the Agent's TUI rather than as a plain shell, and nothing is launched here either
hosts_refresh: POST /api/hosts/:hostId/refresh probes that host through the repository's refresh entry and rescans its session index; data {host_id, refreshed, sessions, detection}; 500 HOST_REFRESH_FAILED keeps the code and reason the repository reported
